questions.stem: What option on the breakdown source record helps provide views into whether you need to create additional breakdowns or adjust data values?

options.text: Security type
Related List Conditions
Label for unmatched
Run Diagnostics

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Label for Unmatched: The 'Label for unmatched' option (C) on the breakdown source record helps provide views into whether additional breakdowns are needed or data values need adjustment. Per p893: This label is applied when the value in a mapped field does not match any elements on the breakdown source — reviewing unmatched records reveals coverage gaps and guides decisions on whether to create additional elements or correct data. Security type (A) controls access. Related List Conditions (B) filters the list. Run Diagnostics (D) is not a breakdown source option.

questions.stem: What data update settings can you enable for a single score visualisation to update the score in real-time?

options.text: Background refresh interval (minutes)
Show score update time
Real time update
Live refresh date (seconds)

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Visualisations > Real-Time Update: The 'Real time update' setting (C) on a single score visualisation updates the score in real-time. Per p959/p1845: 'Enable real-time updating for single score report widgets' — this option is specifically designed for single score widgets to always show the most up-to-date information. Background refresh interval (A) refreshes periodically, not in real-time. Show score update time (B) shows the timestamp. Live refresh date (D) is not a standard field name.

questions.stem: How does KPI Signals support notifications?

options.text: By forwarding email notifications
By automated signal detection jobs
Through regular back-ups
By setting auto-reply responses

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Notifications: KPI Signals supports notifications through automated signal detection jobs (B). Per p664: 'Signals application also has automated signal detection jobs. These jobs send notifications about signals to subscribed users without them having the application open.' For automated indicators, these jobs run whenever a data collection job runs. KPI Signals does not use email forwarding (A), back-ups (C), or auto-reply responses (D) to support notifications.

questions.stem: What 'related lists' are available on the formula indicator form? (Choose three.)

options.text: Targets
Contributing Indicators
Breakdowns
Signals

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > Related Lists: The related lists on the formula indicator form are Targets (A), Contributing Indicators (B), and Breakdowns (C). Contributing Indicators lists the indicators used in the formula. Targets lists global and personal targets. Breakdowns lists applied breakdowns. Per p611: formula indicators display contributing indicators for navigation. Signals (D) is a KPI Signals application feature, not a standard related list on the formula indicator form.

questions.stem: Which of the following visualisation types allow you to add multiple data sources of the same type in the UI Builder? (Choose two.)

options.text: Single Score
Time Series
Pie and donuts
Bars

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Visualisations > Multiple Data Sources: The visualisation types allowing multiple data sources of the same type in UI Builder are Time Series (B) and Bars (D). Per p512: 'All time series — Supported; All bars (horizontal, vertical, Pareto) — Supported; All scores (single score, dial, gauge) — Not supported; Pies and donuts — Not supported.' Single Score (A) and Pie and donuts (C) do not support multiple data sources of the same type in UI Builder.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true about creating User Experience filters? (Choose three.)

options.text: Only users with the admin role can create User Experience filters.
For filters to work in workspaces, you must configure an event handler to apply the filters.
The filter you create in the Now Experience UI Builder is available in all workspaces.
A single filter can be used across all visualisations in a workspace.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > UX Filters > Characteristics: True statements about User Experience filters are: only admin role can create them (A), filters in workspaces require event handler configuration (B), and a single filter can be used across all visualisations in a workspace (D). Per p554: 'you have to create custom event handlers for filters to apply to lists or data visualizations' (B). UX filters operate as global filters 'impacting all visualizations across the entire dashboard' (D). Filters are workspace-specific, not available in all workspaces (C is false).

questions.stem: What calendar type can you use to analyse scores using time periods?

options.text: Team Calendar
Maintenance Calendar
Custom Business Calendar
On-Call Calendar

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Business Calendars > Score Analysis: Custom Business Calendar (C) can be used to analyze scores using custom time periods. Per p831/p832: custom and fiscal calendars allow analyzing indicator scores based on business calendar entries rather than standard calendar periods. The indicator frequency is derived from the business calendar instead of a static list. Team Calendar (A) and On-Call Calendar (D) are for scheduling. Maintenance Calendar (B) is for planned maintenance windows.

questions.stem: What role or access do users need to act on a signal to reset a baseline or dismiss a signal?

options.text: Responsible users without workspace access
Users with the admin, pa_admin, or pa_kpi_signal_admin role without being a responsible user
Only users with the admin role
Users irrespective of their level of responsibility

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Baseline/Dismiss Access: Users with the admin, pa_admin, or pa_kpi_signal_admin role (B) can reset a baseline or dismiss a signal without being a responsible user. Per p659: 'Users with the admin, pa_admin, or pa_kpi_signal_admin role can reset a baseline or dismiss a signal without explicitly being a responsible user. Users with other roles must become responsible users to take action.' Admin alone (C) is not the complete answer. All users (D) cannot act on signals.

questions.stem: Which of the following data update settings for single score visualisations shows the timestamp of when the score was last updated?

options.text: Show score update time
Real time update
Background refresh interval (minutes)
Follow filters

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Visualisations > Score Update Time: The 'Show score update time' setting (A) shows the timestamp of when the score was last updated on a single score visualisation. Per p231: Show score update time displays when the score was collected, providing transparency about data freshness. Real time update (B) enables live data refresh. Background refresh interval (C) sets periodic refresh frequency in minutes. Follow filters (D) makes the visualisation respond to dashboard-level filters.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true statements about configuring pie, donut, and single score visualisations in workspaces?

options.text: Data labels are shown as only percentages, as values, or as both.
Legend percentages are shown along with values.
The metric label name is displayed near the metric value.
Set gradient, texture, or no colour options for data display.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Visualisations > Pie/Donut/Single Score Config: True statements are: data labels shown as percentages, values, or both (A); legend percentages shown with values (B); metric label name displayed near metric value (C). Per p380: 'Show legend value adds the number; Show legend percentage provides more information.' Per p231: 'Show metric label' option is available. Setting gradient, texture, or no colour options (D) is not a standard configuration option for these visualisation types.

questions.stem: What role is required to create personal targets and thresholds for users who can view an indicator on the Analytics Hub?

options.text: pa_viewer
pa_target_admin
pa_threshold_admin
No role

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Roles > Personal Targets: The pa_viewer role (A) is required to create personal targets and thresholds for users who can view an indicator on the Analytics Hub. Per p1088: pa_viewer allows users to 'Read and update scores in scoresheets. View the Analytics Hub' and set personal targets. pa_target_admin (B) and pa_threshold_admin (C) are for creating global targets/thresholds for all users. No role (D) is insufficient for creating personal targets on the Analytics Hub.

questions.stem: Which of the following are suggested when you type in a query on Analytics Q&A? (Choose three.)

options.text: Recent searches
Tables and columns
Breakdowns
Indicators

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Analytics Q&A > Suggestions: When typing in Analytics Q&A, suggestions include Recent searches (A), Tables and columns (B), and Indicators (D). Per p1452/p591: Analytics Q&A 'displays suggestions while you type' based on keywords. It suggests recent search history, available tables/columns for table-based queries, and performance analytics indicators. Breakdowns (C) are associated with indicators but are not primary suggestion categories displayed while typing in Analytics Q&A.

questions.stem: What is an easy way for a responsible user to get real-time updates on the signals for a particular KPI?

options.text: Monitoring the signal score on a dashboard
Receive email notifications
Schedule a report for the signal data
Manually check the KPI doe signals

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Real-Time Updates: The easiest way for a responsible user to get real-time updates on signals is to receive email notifications (B). Per p660: 'a responsible user... still gets email notifications about unresolved signals or actions on signals.' Email reminders are sent automatically whenever signals occur or remain unresolved. Monitoring a dashboard (A) requires active checking. Scheduling a report (C) is periodic. Manually checking (D) requires user action.

questions.stem: How should an admin activate the KPI Signals?

options.text: Raise a ServiceNow Support (HI) request
Request from the ServiceNow Store
It is active by default
Activate the sn-kpi-signals plugin

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Activation: KPI Signals is active by default (C). Per p665: 'KPI Signals is activated by default. If you do not want this feature, request a ServiceNow AI Platform administrator to disable KPI Signals.' No HI request (A), Store installation (B), or separate plugin activation (D) is required. Monitoring for individual indicators must be explicitly activated, but the KPI Signals application itself is enabled by default.

questions.stem: What does anti-signal indicate in KPI Signals?

options.text: No signal has been detected
Long-term stability
Abnormal variation in the scores of a KPI
A workflow has changed

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Anti-Signal: An anti-signal indicates long-term stability (B) — a sustained period where the process behaves consistently within expected bounds. Per p653: 'Although responsible users are notified when an anti-signal is generated, no action is required.' This contrasts with a signal (abnormal variation requiring action) and 'no signal' (shorter period with no detection and no notification). Anti-signals confirm stable process behavior rather than detecting problems or workflow changes.

questions.stem: How do you create and associate breakdowns on the breakdown source form?

options.text: By selecting the ‘New’ button on the ‘Breakdowns’ related list
From the ‘Additional actions’ menu
From the ‘Create Breakdowns’ related link
By adding multiple ‘Facts tables’ under the Source tab

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Create on Source Form: To create and associate breakdowns on the breakdown source form, select the 'New' button on the 'Breakdowns' related list (A). Per p898/p889: the breakdown source form has a Breakdowns related list where new breakdowns can be created and associated directly. The Additional actions menu (B) does not create breakdowns. 'Create Breakdowns' related link (C) is not a standard option. Adding Facts tables (D) defines the data source, not breakdown associations.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used across all the visualisations in a workspace?

options.text: Signal
Dashboard Builder
Studio
User Experience filter

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > UX Filters > Cross-Visualisation Use: User Experience filters (D) can be used across all visualisations in a workspace. Per p554: 'When you enable User Experience Analytics filters within Platform Analytics dashboards, they operate as global filters. This means their effect is comprehensive, impacting all visualizations across the entire dashboard.' Signals (A) are KPI-specific alerts. Dashboard Builder (B) and Studio (C) are development tools, not filters that apply across visualisations.

questions.stem: How are responsible users reminded when a signal remains unresolved?

options.text: Via Virtual Agent
Via Connect Chat
By email notification
By text message

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Signals > Unresolved Reminders: Responsible users are reminded about unresolved signals via email notification (C). Per p660: 'As a responsible user, you receive email reminders about signals that have not been resolved.' The system sends periodic email reminders until the signal is acted upon. Virtual Agent (A) and Connect Chat (B) are not used for signal reminders. Text messages (D) are not a supported notification channel for KPI Signals.

questions.stem: What related list in the formula indicator record is used to navigate to the indicators used in the formula or to their indicator sources?

options.text: Breakdowns
Contributing Indicators
Indicator Groups
Managed Sources

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > Contributing Indicators: The 'Contributing Indicators' related list (B) on the formula indicator record navigates to the indicators used in the formula or their indicator sources. Per p611: 'View contributing indicators to a formula in KPI Details — you can list the contributing indicators to that formula.' Breakdowns (A) shows applied breakdowns. Indicator Groups (C) organizes indicators. Managed Sources (D) is not a standard related list on the formula indicator form.

questions.stem: Which of the following items can you view without the pa_viewer role if the indicator and breakdown ACLs are respected? (Choose two.)

options.text: Diagnostic Results
KPI Details
Analytics Hub
Widget Statistics

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Roles > No Role Access: Users can view KPI Details (B) and the Analytics Hub (C) without the pa_viewer role if indicator and breakdown ACLs are respected. Per p1087: 'No role: View Performance Analytics visuals on the Service Portal. View dashboards that have been shared with this user.' Per p654: 'Role required: Any roles necessary to access the workspace... ACLs for indicators and breakdowns are also respected.' Diagnostic Results (A) and Widget Statistics (D) require appropriate PA roles.

questions.stem: Which of the following styling options is NOT available with the data visualisation component configuration in workspaces?

options.text: Sort on categories in bar, pie, and donut visualisations based on table data sources.
Set default, palette, or single colour options for data display.
Change score sizes of single score visualisations.
Create a new visualisation type with predefined styling.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Visualisations > Styling Options: Creating a new visualisation type with predefined styling (D) is NOT available in the data visualisation component configuration. Per p326: available styling includes color type (Default, Color palette, Single color), score sizes, and sort options. Sort on categories (A), set colour options (B), and change score sizes for single score (C) are all valid styling options. Creating entirely new visualisation types is not a configuration option within the component panel.

questions.stem: Which of the following can you do when you set a target for an indicator on the Analytics Hub? (Choose three.)

options.text: Set the improvement as a percentage.
Set a review date on which to consider updating the target.
Set the threshold as an improvement on the average score.
Set a start date in the future.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Targets > Analytics Hub Options: When setting a target on the Analytics Hub, you can set the improvement as a percentage (A), set a review date to consider updating the target (B), and set a start date in the future (D). Per p947/p632: targets support percentage/unit improvements, review dates, and future start dates. Setting a threshold as an improvement on the average score (C) describes threshold configuration, not target configuration — these are separate features.

questions.stem: What condition do you use on the Elements Filter record for the ‘Groups’ Breakdown Source to get only groups that had an incident assigned to them?

options.text: By adding ‘itil’ to the Roles necessary to see the filter
By adding ‘Incident->Assignment group’ to the Related List Conditions
By adding ‘itil’ type to the ‘Conditions’
By selecting ‘Incident [incident]’ for the Facts table

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Elements Filters > Related List Conditions: To get only groups that had an incident assigned to them, add 'Incident->Assignment group' to the Related List Conditions (B) on the Elements Filter record for the Groups breakdown source. Per p908: element filter fields include Related List Conditions to filter breakdown elements by their relationship to other tables. Adding itil to Roles (A/C) controls who can see the filter, not which groups are included. Facts table (D) is on the breakdown source, not the elements filter.

questions.stem: Which system property enables an administrator to allow specified user roles to select indicators as data sources from the Data Visualisation Configuration panel?

options.text: glide.knowman.search.apply_role_based_security
par_vis_config.data_source.can_select_indicator
com.snc.pa.dc.max_row_count_indicator_source
glide.source_control.checksum_required

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Properties > Indicator Selection Role: The par_vis_config.data_source.can_select_indicator property (B) enables administrators to specify which user roles can select indicators as data sources from the Data Visualization Configuration panel. Per p552: 'par_vis_config.data_source.can_select_indicator: Specifies roles (comma-separated) which can select indicators as data sources from the Data Visualization configuration panel. If empty, all users can select.' The other properties control knowledge base security, row counts, and source control.

questions.stem: You have created a new Breakdown. When trying to associate the new Breakdown to existing Indicators, you see that no Indicators are available. What might be the issue preventing you from adding the indicators to the new Breakdown?

options.text: The indicator facts table is not included in the Breakdown mappings.
The Indicators are configured incorrectly.
Custom tables do not allow Breakdowns.
The Breakdown field is not on the form for the facts table.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Association Issue: No indicators appear when associating a new breakdown because the indicator facts table is not included in the breakdown mappings (A). Per p888/p889: 'You can apply the breakdown to other indicators with the same source table as the indicator you selected first. If the breakdown already applies to an indicator, that indicator is not displayed.' Breakdowns can only be associated with indicators that share the same facts table. Incorrect indicators (B), custom tables (C), and form fields (D) are not the cause.

questions.stem: As a Performance Analytics Admin, what is the best course of action after running Diagnostics?

options.text: Review the suggested solution and take steps to resolve the error or warning.
Review the linked knowledge base article.
For errors, use the Create a Problem UI action to create a problem record.
Contact the system administrator if any errors or warnings are generated.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Diagnostics > Post-Run Action: After running Diagnostics, the best course of action is to review the suggested solution and take steps to resolve the error or warning (A). Per p1025: 'If a diagnostic returns a warning or error, review the provided solution and take steps to resolve the issue.' Reviewing a knowledge article (B) is supplementary. Creating a Problem record (C) is not the standard action. Contacting the system administrator (D) is not needed since the admin IS running diagnostics.

questions.stem: Select the role that lets you create and configure Indicators and Breakdowns, and manage Data collection.

options.text: PA Power User
PA Admin
PA Data Collector
PA Contributor

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Roles > PA Admin: The PA Admin role (B) lets you create and configure Indicators and Breakdowns, and manage Data collection. PA Admin has full access to all Performance Analytics configuration including indicator creation, breakdown creation/configuration, and data collection job management. PA Power User (A) cannot create breakdown sources. PA Data Collector (C) collects data but has limited configuration access. PA Contributor (D) is a basic contributor role without full admin capabilities.

questions.stem: In KPI Details, what happens when an indicator is forecasted to hit a future target?

options.text: A new target is automatically set as an improvement of the current target
The KPI status is set to On Track
A comment is automatically generated
The target owner is prompted to set a new Target Review date

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Details > Target Forecast: When an indicator is forecasted to hit a future target in KPI Details, a comment is automatically generated (C) to acknowledge the achievement. Per p630: the status icon updates to show 'On track' when the forecast predicts the target will be met. A new target (A) is not automatically set. KPI status icon (B) updates to On Track but this is not what 'happens' as an action. The target owner (D) is not automatically prompted — review dates are manually configured.

questions.stem:
You wish to hide the 1- Critical priority incidents for itil users viewing the dashboard.
Select the required Breakdown Source security configuration.

options.text: Security type: Blacklist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical
Security type: Whitelist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Blacklist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Whitelist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Security > Deny/Blacklist: To HIDE 1-Critical priority incidents from itil users, use Security type: Blacklist (Deny list) with Roles: itil and Elements: 1-Critical (A). Per p917: 'Deny list: Exclude groups and users with the roles you specify from seeing the specified elements.' A Whitelist for itil with 1-Critical (D) would show ONLY 1-Critical to itil users, which is the opposite. Whitelist with All roles and other elements (B) would hide Critical from everyone. Blacklist with All roles and other elements (C) would hide non-Critical from everyone.

questions.stem: What does the number of “Inserts” represent in a Job Log record?

options.text: The sum of the stored scores
Number of Indicator Source records examined
The number on incidents inserted into the instance yesterday
Number of Performance Analytics scores stored

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Job Logs > Inserts: The number of 'Inserts' in a Job Log record represents the number of Performance Analytics scores stored (D) — the new score records inserted into the PA scores table during that collection job. Per p1013: 'Inserts: The number of new records that [are stored].' This represents newly computed and saved scores, not the sum of stored scores (A), indicator source records examined (B), or incident records inserted (C).

questions.stem: Which should you implement to obtain insights on new and returning platform users and their navigation patterns?

options.text: User Experience Analytics
Next Experience Dashboards
Responsive Dashboards
Platform Analytics Workspace

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > User Experience Analytics > Navigation Insights: User Experience Analytics (A) provides insights on new and returning platform users and their navigation patterns. Per p1118: UEA supports 'Tracking specific users or tracking users with specific roles' and provides analytics on user behavior, navigation, and session data. Next Experience Dashboards (B) and Responsive Dashboards (C) display data but do not analyze user navigation patterns. Platform Analytics Workspace (D) is for data visualization management.

questions.stem: What configuration is required to use a Breakdown as a filter for Report Widgets?

options.text: Configure the Dashboard Breakdown to act as Interactive Filter.
Breakdowns automatically filter report widgets so nothing needs to be done.
Edit the report widget to select the Breakdown to apply.
Create a separate dashboard for report widgets and apply the desired Breakdown in the dashboard properties.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Dashboards > Breakdown as Filter: To use a Breakdown as a filter for report widgets, configure the Dashboard Breakdown to act as an Interactive Filter (A). Per p1930: the breakdown source has an 'Act as filter' option that enables it to function as an interactive filter on dashboards. Per p1931: report widgets then follow the interactive filter. Breakdowns (B) do not automatically filter report widgets. Editing the widget (C) selects what to display, not how it filters. Creating a separate dashboard (D) is not required.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes Performance Analytics Spotlight?

options.text: A rank list of records based on several weighted conditions
A visualization of an indicator score to display on a dashboard
A view of the record priority at the current time
A view of the process data captured over a period of time

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Spotlight > Description: Performance Analytics Spotlight is a rank list of records based on several weighted conditions (A). Per p983: 'Ranking records with Spotlight' — Spotlight creates a prioritized/ranked list of records scored by multiple weighted criteria to surface the most important items. It is not a visualisation for a dashboard (B), a view of current record priority (C), or a time-series view of process data (D) — those describe other PA features.

questions.stem: Select all statements that accurately describe the Platform Analytics Workspace / Analytics Center application. (Choose two.)

options.text: The Analytics Center replaces the classic Performance Analytics application.
The Platform Analytics Workspace is a paid application.
The Platform Analytics Workspace lets you manage Next Experience data visualizations and dashboards.
You can configure the Analytics Center to be accessible from any ServiceNow Workspace.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Platform Analytics Workspace > True Statements: True statements are that Platform Analytics Workspace is a paid application (B) and that it lets you manage Next Experience data visualizations and dashboards (C). Per p10: 'The Platform Analytics experience is a unified interface for visualizing data.' Analytics Center does not replace the classic PA application (A is false) — it coexists with it. While Analytics Center can be added to workspaces (D is partially true per p591), this is not a defining characteristic like B and C.

questions.stem: You plan to collect historical data for the default indicator “Number of open and overdue incidents.” Which breakdown should be excluded from the historical data collection job?

options.text: Category
Age
State
Priority

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Data Collection > Historical Exclusion: The Priority breakdown (D) should be excluded from historical data collection for open/overdue incidents because priority can change over time — historical scores would not accurately reflect the priority at the historical date. Per p981: you can exclude specific breakdowns from historical collection jobs. Category (A), Age (B), and State (C) are also time-sensitive but Priority is the most commonly excluded because it is frequently changed after incident creation.

questions.stem: What are the default Access Control options for a new Indicator?

options.text: Visible to Just Me. Visible by All Roles is False, role required is pa_admin.
Visible to Everyone. Visible by All Roles is True.
Visible to Everyone. Visible by All Roles is False, role required is pa_admin.
Visible to Just Me. Visible by All Roles is False.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicators > Default Access Control: New indicators default to Visible to Everyone with Visible by All Roles set to True (B). By default, when a new indicator is created, it is accessible to all users without role restrictions. Restricting visibility by roles (A, C, D) must be explicitly configured after creation. This open-by-default approach ensures new indicators are immediately usable and visible across the platform until administrators apply targeted restrictions.

questions.stem:
You wish to show only the 1 - Critical incidents to itil users viewing the dashboard.
Select the required Breakdown Source security configuration.

options.text: Security type: Whitelist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Blacklist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Whitelist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical
Security type: Blacklist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Security > Whitelist: To show ONLY 1-Critical incidents to itil users, use Security type: Whitelist (Allow list) with Roles: itil and Elements: 1-Critical (C). Per p917: a Whitelist means only users with the specified roles can see the specified elements; all other roles see nothing for this breakdown. A Blacklist for itil with 1-Critical (D) would HIDE 1-Critical from itil users. Whitelist with All roles and non-Critical elements (A) would show non-Critical to all. Blacklist with non-Critical (B) would hide non-Critical from everyone.

questions.stem: What is the best practice to manage deprecated Homepages?

options.text: Manually recreate the affected Homepages as Dashboards
Use the “Convert to Dashboard” UI Action
Use the “Copy as Dashboard” UI Action
Use the “Unload to Dashboard” UI Action

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Dashboards > Homepage Migration: The best practice to manage deprecated Homepages is to use the 'Convert to Dashboard' UI Action (B). Per p1899/p1900: 'Convert homepages to dashboards' — the convert flow creates a new dashboard from the homepage, moves permissions, and closes the homepage record. Per p1900: 'Users no longer have access to converted homepages. They can find the dashboard versions.' Manually recreating (A) is inefficient. Copy as Dashboard (C) and Unload to Dashboard (D) are not standard UI Actions for this purpose.

questions.stem: Which feature can be used to view all Indicators used by a widget and all of the Tabs a widget appears on?

options.text: Run Diagnostics
Dependency Assessment
Relationship Viewer
Widget Indicators

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Dependency Assessment > Widget View: The Dependency Assessment feature (B) is used to view all Indicators used by a widget and all the Tabs a widget appears on. Per p1026: 'Use the Dependency Assessment tree view to view and edit Performance Analytics components including widgets, indicators, and breakdowns.' It provides a full dependency map of PA components. Run Diagnostics (A) checks for configuration issues. Relationship Viewer (C) is a CMDB feature. Widget Indicators (D) is not a standard PA feature name.

questions.stem:
Consider this scenario:
1. You are working with a default ServiceNow instance.
2. You need to configure a Breakdown source and a Breakdown for the Close code field in order to analyze incident data by Close codes.

Which of the following is the correct Facts table to use in the Breakdown source for Close code?

options.text: Close Code [sys_close_code]
Choice [sys_choice]
Incident [incident]
Task [task]

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Close Code Facts Table: The correct facts table for a Close code breakdown source is Choice [sys_choice] (B). Per p889: 'For example, the Incident.Category breakdown source takes its elements from the Choice table. The elements are identified by the Sys ID field.' Close code is a choice field on Incident, so its elements come from the Choice [sys_choice] table filtered by table=incident and element=close_code. Close Code (A) is not a separate table. Incident (C) and Task (D) are the indicator source tables, not the breakdown source table.

questions.stem: After modifying a Dashboard created from another Dashboard using the “Duplicate Dashboard” functionality, what type of changes are visible on both the original and the duplicate Dashboard going forward?

options.text: Layout
Any changes to Widgets made with the Edit Content icon
Tab names and order
Changes to the “Follow Interactive Filter” setting

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Dashboards > Duplicate Dashboard: After duplicating a dashboard, changes to Widgets made with the Edit Content icon (B) are visible on both the original and duplicate because widgets are shared between the two dashboards — editing the widget content affects the shared widget record. Layout changes (A), tab names and order (C), and Follow Interactive Filter settings (D) are per-dashboard configurations that are independent after duplication and do not affect both dashboards.

questions.stem: Select the valid Performance Analytics Widget types. (Choose two.)

options.text: Pie
Time Series
Heatmap
Breakdown

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Widget Types > Valid Types: Valid Performance Analytics Widget types are Time Series (B) and Breakdown (D). Per p1948: PA widget types include Score widget (latest/speedometer/real-time), List widget (scorecard/spider web), Time Series (compare/line/Pareto), and Breakdown (scorecard per breakdown element). Pie (A) is a report/visualization type, not a PA widget type. Heatmap (C) is a visualization used inside Pivot widgets but is not itself a PA widget type.

questions.stem: What must be true in order to apply the same Breakdown to Indicators using different facts tables?

options.text: The Breakdown and Indicators must belong to the same application scope.
All Indicators must belong to the same data collection job.
Breakdown Relations must be configured between the included Indicators.
A Breakdown Mapping must be configured for each facts table.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Multiple Facts Tables: To apply the same Breakdown to Indicators using different facts tables, a Breakdown Mapping must be configured for each facts table (D). Per p889: breakdowns can be associated with indicators that share the same source table via breakdown mappings — each different facts table requires its own mapping configuration. Same application scope (A) and same data collection job (B) are not required. Breakdown Relations (C) are for navigating hierarchical data, not for cross-table breakdown association.

questions.stem: In KPI Details, what happens when an indicator misses its target on the Target Review date?

options.text: The KPI status is set to Missed.
The KPI status is set to Not Met.
The associated target is disabled.
The KPI status is set to Off Track.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > KPI Details > Missed Target: When an indicator misses its target on the Target Review date, the KPI status is set to Not Met (B). Per p630: forecast statuses are 'On track, Off track, or Too early to track.' When the actual review date arrives and the score is below the target, the target status becomes 'Not Met.' Missed (A) is not a standard KPI status. The target (C) is not disabled automatically. Off Track (D) is a forecast status before the review date, not the final status when the target is missed.

questions.stem: A Performance Analytics Widget does not follow the Dashboard Breakdown Source. Select the possible reasons for this behavior. (Choose three.)

options.text: It is a time series type widget.
The Indicator in the Widget has no configured Breakdowns.
“Follow Element” is not checked in the Widget data settings.
The Widget is prevented from seeing the data due to Element security.
The Breakdown used by the Widget is using a different Breakdown Source.
The Widget is configured to follow an Interactive Filter.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Dashboards > Widget Not Following Breakdown: Reasons a widget does not follow the Dashboard Breakdown Source are: the Indicator has no configured breakdowns (B), Follow Element is not checked in widget data settings (C), and element security prevents seeing the data (D). Per p1997: 'Follow element' must be selected for the widget to follow dashboard breakdown elements. Per p919: element security restricts breakdown visibility. Per p927: widgets without breakdowns cannot apply a dashboard breakdown.

questions.stem: Select the allowed visualization type for Text Analytics Widgets.

options.text: Keyword List
Breakdown
Word Cloud
Time series

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Text Analytics > Visualization Type: The allowed visualization type for Text Analytics Widgets is Word Cloud (C). Per p2044: 'In the Type field, select Text. Word Cloud is automatically selected as the Visualization.' Text analytics widgets visualize word frequencies and groupings from text entered in forms. Keyword List (A) and Breakdown (D) are not text analytics visualization types. Time series (D) shows indicator scores over time, not text analysis.

questions.stem:
An Active Collection Job is configured as follows:
• Relative start: 0 days ago
• Relative end: 0 days ago
• Run: Daily

Which scores will be collected for a Daily Indicator included in this job?

options.text: Scores for Tomorrow
Scores for Today
The job fails and no scores are collected
Scores for Yesterday

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Data Collection > Collection Period: With relative start and end both set to 0 days ago and run Daily, scores for Today (B) will be collected. Per p978: 0 days ago = today. The job collects data for the current date. Per p978: 'Daily scheduled jobs normally should collect for the most recently completed day... they should have both a relative start and relative end of one day ago.' Using 0 days ago collects today's data, not yesterday's (D).

questions.stem: Which Breakdown Source attribute becomes visible and disabled when the number of Breakdown elements exceeds the maximum allowed as defined in the System Properties?

options.text: Collection error
Dependency Assessment
DC active
Run Diagnostics

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Sources > Element Limit: The 'DC active' attribute (C) becomes visible and disabled on a Breakdown Source when the number of breakdown elements exceeds the maximum allowed in System Properties. Per p1101: 'When the number of elements with scores reaches this limit, the breakdown source is disabled.' The DC active field indicates whether data collection is active for the breakdown source and is automatically disabled when the element limit is exceeded.

questions.stem: You have a Daily Collection job. How should you configure Relative start and Relative end to be able to collect scores for yesterday?

options.text: 1 days ago to 0 days ago
-1 days ago to 0 days ago
0 days ago to 0 days ago
1 days ago to 1 days ago

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Data Collection > Yesterday's Scores: To collect scores for yesterday with a Daily collection job, set both Relative start and Relative end to 1 days ago (D). Per p978: 'Daily scheduled jobs normally should collect for the most recently completed day. Therefore, they should have both a relative start and relative end of one day ago.' 0 days ago collects today (B). Mixing 1 days ago and 0 days ago (A) would collect a range spanning yesterday and today.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Direction property of an Indicator?

options.text: Sets the layout of the Indicator when used on a Dashboard
Helps determine the order the Indicator appears on lists
Determines whether a score is rounded up or down
Indicates whether scores should ideally increase or decrease

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicators > Direction Property: The Direction property indicates whether scores should ideally increase or decrease (D). Per p868: 'If you prefer that the score of this indicator increases or decreases over time, select Maximize or Minimize in the Direction field. Analytical tools and graphic displays use this Direction with this indicator.' It does not set layout (A), order in lists (B), or rounding behavior (C). Key indicators should always have Maximize or Minimize set.

questions.stem: How can you tell that an Automated Breakdown is using a Bucket Group?

options.text: The Facts table of the Breakdown is set to [pa_buckets].
The Default elements filter of the Breakdown specifies the Bucket Groups.
The Facts table of the Breakdown Source is set to [pa_buckets].
The Related list conditions of the Breakdown Source identify the Bucket Groups.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Bucket Group Identification: An Automated Breakdown using a Bucket Group has its Facts table of the Breakdown Source set to [pa_buckets] (C). Per p756/p896: 'create a breakdown source that uses Bucket [pa_buckets] as the facts table' to work with bucket groups. The bucket group is then specified in the breakdown source conditions. The breakdown's own Facts table (A) would be different. Default elements filter (B) does not identify bucket groups. Related list conditions (D) are not used for bucket group identification.

questions.stem:
In your data model, there is a relationship between the Assigned To user and their Manager.
Breakdown Relations use this relationship that is current as of?

options.text: When the Breakdown Relation is updated
When the Breakdown Relations job is executed
When the Data Collector is executed
When the Indicator is viewed

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Relations > Currency: Breakdown Relations use the relationship that is current as of when the Indicator is viewed (D). The relationship between records (such as Assigned To user and their Manager) is resolved dynamically at view time, reflecting the current state of that relationship. This means if a manager changes, the breakdown relation shows the current manager. The relation is not frozen at when the relation record is updated (A), job execution (B), or data collection (C).

questions.stem: Select the syntactically INCORRECT formula, assuming that all Indicators names are valid.

options.text: ((Number of new critical incidents)) / ((Number of new incidents)) * 100
100 - ((([[Average resolution time of resolved incidents]] - 17.5) / 17.5) * 100)
if ([[Number of resolved incidents]] == 0) {0} else ([[Number of resolved incidents]])
[[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > Incorrect Syntax: The syntactically incorrect formula is A: ((Number of new critical incidents)) / ((Number of new incidents)) * 100. Per PA formula syntax, indicator names must be wrapped in [[ ]] for indicator references or {{ }} for aggregate scores. Using (( )) double parentheses around indicator names (A) is not valid PA formula syntax. B, C, and D all use correct syntax — [[ ]] for indicator references and {{ }} for aggregate/total scores.

questions.stem: Which Indicator should you exclude from a Historic Data Collection because its scores cannot be accurately collected?

options.text: Number of incidents resolved in time
Number of open problems not updated in last 90 days
Number of new requests
Summed age of open problems

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Historical Collection > Exclusion: 'Number of open problems not updated in last 90 days' (B) should be excluded from Historic Data Collection because its condition uses a relative time filter ('last 90 days') that cannot be accurately evaluated for historical dates. When collecting data historically, relative time conditions are calculated against the historical collection date, but whether problems were 'not updated' 90 days before a historical date cannot be determined accurately from current data.

questions.stem:
Consider the example formula below. What is the formula output when a Breakdown is applied?

[[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100;

options.text: The formula compares the current score to the previous score.
The formula returns the Breakdown score as a percentage of the overall score.
The formula returns 100.
The formula compares each Time series to the default Time series.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > Breakdown Percentage: The formula [[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100 returns the Breakdown score as a percentage of the overall score (B). [[ ]] returns the score filtered by the applied breakdown element; {{ }} returns the aggregate total score regardless of breakdown. When divided and multiplied by 100, the result shows what percentage of the total the breakdown element represents. This compares breakdown to total, not to previous scores (A) or time series (D).

questions.stem: Which is a true statement about a Formula Indicator?

options.text: Any formula errors are reported in the Formula Error log.
The Formula Indicator uses a Performance Analytics Script.
The Formula Indicator score is calculated at collection time.
The code in the Formula box is JavaScript.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > JavaScript: The code in the Formula box of a Formula Indicator is JavaScript (D). Per p1075: Performance Analytics formula indicators use JavaScript syntax with PA-specific variables and methods. Formulas reference indicators using [[ ]] and {{ }} notation within JavaScript code. Formula errors (A) are reported in data collection job logs, not a separate Formula Error log. PA Scripts (B) are separate from formula indicators. Formula scores (C) are calculated at collection time, but this is a property of data collection, not a characteristic of the formula language.

questions.stem: Which of these Indicators should NOT be included in a Historical Collection? (Choose two.)

options.text: Average age of open incidents
Number of new incidents
Number of incidents not updated in the last 5 days
Number of incidents with no assignment group

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Historical Collection > Exclusions: Indicators NOT to include in Historical Collection are Average age of open incidents (A) and Number of incidents not updated in last 5 days (C). Both use relative time-based conditions that cannot be accurately computed for historical dates: 'age' would be calculated from collection date (not the historical date), and 'not updated in last 5 days' is relative to the historical date and cannot be verified from current data. Number of new incidents (B) and incidents with no assignment group (D) can be accurately collected historically.

questions.stem: Which of the following measurements can be obtained using Reporting? (Choose two.)

options.text: Weekly comparison of Incident resolution time vs SLA met percentage
Forecast of HR Case Resolution Times over the Next Month
Currently Active Incidents with Open Problems
Current view of Employees by Department
Department Headcount Over Time

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Reporting vs PA > Measurement Types: Currently Active Incidents with Open Problems (C) and Current view of Employees by Department (D) can be obtained using Reporting. These are point-in-time snapshots of current table data — exactly what Reporting provides. Weekly comparison of resolution time vs SLA (A) and Department Headcount Over Time (E) require time-series trending data — better obtained from Performance Analytics. Forecast of HR Case Resolution Times (B) requires forecasting functionality available in Performance Analytics, not basic Reporting.

questions.stem: What is the best way to limit the exponential growth of Breakdown element scores?

options.text: By consolidating Breakdowns
By unchecking the “Collect breakdown matrix” property of an indicator
By defining no more than 2 Breakdowns
By changing the value of “Maximum number of breakdown elements in scorecard lists” property

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Exponential Score Growth: To limit exponential growth of Breakdown element scores, uncheck the 'Collect breakdown matrix' property of an indicator (B). Breakdown matrix collection creates scores for ALL combinations of two breakdowns, which grows exponentially. Per p862/p1102: with two breakdowns of 100 elements each, the matrix creates up to 10,000 combinations. Unchecking this property prevents matrix collection. Consolidating breakdowns (A) or limiting to 2 breakdowns (C) reduces scope but does not address the root cause. The maximum elements property (D) limits storage but does not prevent exponential growth.

questions.stem: How is an Indicator Source used in data collection?

options.text: Collect all the matching records into a temporary result set
Build the first half of an encoded query
Create a new Scores table for the selected Facts table
Act as a folder to keep similar indicators together

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicator Sources > Data Collection Use: An Indicator Source is used in data collection to collect all matching records into a temporary result set (A). The indicator source defines the facts table and conditions; during collection, the data collector queries the table with those conditions to gather matching records, then calculates aggregate scores from that temporary set. It builds a full query (not just the first half - B is wrong), does not create a new Scores table (C), and is not a folder for organization (D).

questions.stem: When configuring an Interactive Filter on a dashboard, how do you ensure that Report widgets will be filtered correctly.

options.text: Edit each widget and enable “Apply Dashboard Filter”
Edit each widget and enable “Follow element”
For each widget, enable “Act as interactive filter”
For each widget, enable “Follow interactive filter”

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Interactive Filters > Report Widget Setup: To ensure report widgets are filtered correctly when configuring an Interactive Filter, edit each widget and enable 'Follow interactive filter' (D). Per p1931: 'This option is available for all report widgets... select Follow interactive filter.' Per p1920: 'Select the Edit widget icon on each visualization that should follow the filter and select Follow interactive filter.' Apply Dashboard Filter (A) and Follow element (B) are for PA widgets. Act as interactive filter (C) is configured on the filter, not the widget.

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios require the use of a scripted Breakdown Mapping? (Choose two.)

options.text: Categorizing Requests based on the number of times they were updated.
Categorizing the length of time since Tasks were updated into Age Ranges.
Categorizing Incidents based on their Priority.
Categorizing Tasks based on the Hour of the Day they were created.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Mappings > Script Required: Scripted Breakdown Mappings are needed for categorizing the length of time since tasks updated into Age Ranges (B) — requires calculating elapsed duration; and categorizing tasks by Hour of Day they were created (D) — requires extracting the hour from a datetime field. Both require scripts since no direct field contains those calculated values. Priority (C) is a simple direct field reference requiring no script. Categorizing by number of updates (A) would also need a script but B and D are the most clearly scripted scenarios.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an On-click behavior configuration in a Performance Analytics Widget?

options.text: Enable real-time data updates to the widget
Add a secondary Y-axis to the widget chart
Navigate to an external URL instead of the Analytics Hub
Navigate to a URL within the ServiceNow instance instead of the Analytics Hub

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Widgets > On-Click Behavior: The on-click behavior configuration in a PA widget allows navigation to a URL within the ServiceNow instance instead of the default Analytics Hub (D). Per p2054/p2055: 'By default, clicking a widget opens the detailed Analytics Hub. You can configure a widget to navigate to a URL. Only URLs relative to the instance URL are allowed.' It does not enable real-time updates (A), add a secondary Y-axis (B), or navigate to external URLs (C).

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Field attribute on a Breakdown Source form?

options.text: Defines the relationship between the corresponding Breakdown and Indicators
Provides security for the Breakdown values based on user permissions
Limits the number of values returned by the Breakdown Source
Identifies the field that contains a unique value for every record for the breakdown source facts table

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Sources > Field Attribute: The Field attribute on a Breakdown Source form identifies the field that contains a unique value for every record in the breakdown source facts table (D). Per p889/p891: 'Always use a facts table with a field that has a unique value for every record, usually Sys ID.' This unique field is used to identify and distinguish breakdown elements. It does not define relationships between breakdowns and indicators (A), provide security (B), or limit the number of values returned (C).

questions.stem: Select the statements which correctly describe the respective Performance Analytics object behavior. (Choose two.)

options.text: The frequency of an Indicator can differ from that of an Indicator Source
Data collection must be completed before assigning Breakdowns to an Indicator
Breakdowns require a Breakdown Mapping to be added to an Automated Indicator
Indicator Sources with a Monthly frequency can still be collected in a Daily job

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > PA Objects > Behavior Statements: True statements are: Breakdowns require a Breakdown Mapping to be added to an Automated Indicator (C), and Indicator Sources with Monthly frequency can still be collected in a Daily job (D). Per p906: 'The breakdown must have a breakdown mapping for the indicator source table' before associating with indicators. A daily job can include monthly indicators; it generates new scores only when the monthly period changes. Frequency can differ from the source (A is false). Data collection does not need to complete before assigning breakdowns (B is false).

questions.stem: After importing an Update set from another instance, the Indicators, Breakdowns, and Jobs are imported correctly, but all of the Dashboards are completely empty. What is the most likely cause of this?

options.text: The user does not have permissions to view the Dashboard.
The Data Collection jobs have not finished running.
The Widgets are corrupted.
“Unload Dashboard” was not performed before migrating the Update set.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Update Sets > Dashboard Migration: Dashboards are empty after importing an Update Set because 'Unload Dashboard' was not performed before migrating (D). Per p78: 'Dashboard tabs aren't automatically transferred in update sets. You can add a dashboard's components to update sets from a dashboard record using the Unload Dashboard function.' Permissions (A) would show the dashboard with content, not empty. Data collection jobs (B) affect scores, not dashboard structure. Widget corruption (C) would cause errors, not simply empty dashboards.

questions.stem:
You have the following configuration:
• Indicator Average age open incidents with two Breakdowns:
o Assignment Group Manager
o Assignment Group

You have this new requirement:
• When navigating the Average age open incidents Indicator and drilling into an Assignment Group Manager Breakdown element, the viewer should see the groups managed by the selected manager.

Which is the best way to achieve the desired result?

options.text: Create a Breakdown relation between the Assignment Group Manager and the Assignment Group breakdowns.
Create a separate Indicator for each manager and apply additional conditions to the Indicator to only include incidents where they are the Assignment Group manager.
Create a script that runs against the Breakdown, where the elements are filtered to show only the manager’s groups.
Modify the “Average age open incidents” Indicator to add an additional condition that applies a dynamic filter, based on the logged in manager.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Relations > Manager-Group Navigation: The best way to show groups managed by a selected manager when drilling down is to create a Breakdown Relation between the Assignment Group Manager and Assignment Group breakdowns (A). Per p913/p914: Breakdown Relations create navigational connections between breakdowns, allowing users to navigate from one breakdown element (manager) to its related elements (groups managed). Creating separate indicators per manager (B) or dynamic filters (C/D) are impractical and not the intended approach for breakdown navigation.

questions.stem: Select the statement which correctly returns the global target.

options.text: pa.getTarget([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.getTargetGap([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.getGlobalTarget($[[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.Target([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > Global Target Syntax: The correct syntax to return the global target is pa.getGlobalTarget($[[Number of open incidents]], score_end) (C). Per p860/p867: the PA API uses pa.getGlobalTarget() with the $ prefix followed by [[ ]] notation for indicator reference. pa.getTarget() (A) is not the correct method name. pa.getTargetGap() (B) returns the gap between score and target. pa.Target() (D) is not a valid API method. The $ prefix before [[ ]] is required.

questions.stem: The scores of an Automated Indicator are correct as of:

options.text: Most recent Collection time
The time the indicator is viewed
Midnight local time
Midnight UTC

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Automated Indicators > Score Currency: The scores of an Automated Indicator are correct as of the most recent collection time (A). Automated indicators collect scores via scheduled data collection jobs that run at defined intervals. The score represents the state of data at the moment the job ran, not when viewed. Viewing an indicator (B) reads the last stored score — it does not recollect data. Real-time indicators update at view time, but standard automated indicators reflect the most recent collection job run.

questions.stem:
An Indicator stores the value 4250.2.

If the Precision is set to 2, what is displayed in a Score widget?

options.text: 4k

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicators > Score Display with Precision: With Precision set to 2 and a value of 4250.2, the score displays as 4.250.20 (D) — showing two decimal places with a thousands separator. Per p881: an indicator with Precision 2 rounds to the nearest two decimal places (4250.2 becomes 4250.20). The thousands separator formats it as 4.250.20 in some locale settings. Values above 10,000 would use letter abbreviations (4.25k) but 4250.2 is below this threshold so abbreviation does not apply.

questions.stem: What happens when Collect records is enabled on the Indicator form?

options.text: A preview of the records that match the condition is displayed.
A list of sys_ids is stored during collection to allow drill down to records.
An ad-hoc job runs to collect the scores immediately for testing purposes.
An exact copy of the matching records are retained for future reference.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicators > Collect Records: When 'Collect records' is enabled on the Indicator form, a list of sys_ids is stored during collection to allow drill-down to the underlying records (B). This enables users to click on a score in the Analytics Hub or KPI Details and see the actual records that contributed to that score. A preview of matching records (A) is available via Test/Preview buttons, not Collect records. An ad-hoc job (C) is separate functionality. Records are not copied or retained as duplicates (D).

questions.stem:
Consider the following configurations and requirements:
• You plan to set up an Indicator, Average Assignment Duration, to trend the duration of time Resolved Incidents are assigned to Assignment Groups.
• There is an existing metric called Assignment Group which already tracks the duration of time an Incident is assigned to different Assignment Groups.

How would you configure the Indicator Source for the Average Assignment Duration Indicator?

options.text: Facts table: Incident Metric | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Value is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident Metric | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Value is Assignment Group

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Indicator Sources > Metric-Based Configuration: The correct Indicator Source configuration is Facts table: Incident Metric with Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group (A). The Incident Metric table stores time-based assignment group tracking data. The Definition condition filters for the specific Assignment Group metric definition. Options B and C using the Incident table directly would not capture assignment durations. Option D uses the wrong condition (Value instead of Definition for identifying the metric type).

questions.stem:
The formula for % of incidents resolved by first assigned group is configured as follows:

([[ Number of resolved incidents by first assigned group ]] / [[ Number of resolved incidents ]]) * 100

You observe “No Score” whenever the value of Number of resolved incidents component indicator is 0.

What can be done to enhance the formula so it returns 0 instead of “No Score” when there are no resolved incidents?

options.text: Add a conditional JavaScript statement in the formula to return 0 if the value of Number of Resolved Incidents is 0.
Enable the property “Allow formula component to be NULL”.
Set the property “Value when nil” to 0.
Enable the property “Render continuous lines”.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Formula Indicators > NULL Handling: To return 0 instead of 'No Score' when the Number of Resolved Incidents is 0, enable 'Allow formula component to be NULL' (B). Per p865: when this property is enabled, the formula can use null contributing indicators without returning 'No Score' for the entire formula — allowing conditional null value handling. A conditional JavaScript statement (A) could also work but is not the standard PA approach. 'Value when nil' (C) and 'Render continuous lines' (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Select the role which can create new Interactive Filters.

options.text: pa_admin
pa_power_user
report_admin
interactive_filter_user

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Interactive Filters > Creation Role: The report_admin role (C) can create new Interactive Filters. Per p1920: creating interactive filters requires report-level admin access for managing filter records and their configurations. report_admin controls report and dashboard filter creation. pa_admin (A) manages PA indicators and breakdowns, not interactive filter creation. pa_power_user (B) has limited PA object creation but not interactive filter management. interactive_filter_user (D) is not a standard ServiceNow role.

questions.stem: As a good practice, Historical Collection should be configured to run:

options.text: Weekly
Daily
Monthly
Once or On Demand

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Data Collection > Historical Job Schedule: Historical Collection should be configured to run Once or On Demand (D). Per p978/p979: 'Run historical data collection jobs, which have longer collection periods, only once. Schedule the job to run On demand.' Historical jobs collect past data and should only run once during initial setup to avoid overwriting existing correct scores. Running Weekly (A), Daily (B), or Monthly (C) would repeatedly overwrite historical data with each execution, corrupting the stored history.

questions.stem: When is a script required to perform a Breakdown Mapping for a Breakdown based on a Bucket group?

options.text: When there is no field in the indicator Facts table that matches the value to be bucketed
When mapping to a Manual Indicator
When needing to limit the visibility of the Buckets
When the Breakdown is a Manual Breakdown

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Bucket Groups > Script Requirement: A script is required to perform a Breakdown Mapping for a Bucket group Breakdown when there is no field in the indicator facts table that directly matches the value to be bucketed (A). Per p894: 'When you have a breakdown mapping script that collects a range of values, you can define a bucket group.' When the bucket value must be calculated (e.g., elapsed time) rather than read from an existing field, a script is necessary. For direct field matches, a simple field-based mapping works without scripting.

questions.stem: When using Text Analytics in Performance Analytics, what fields are analyzed?

options.text: All Journal fields on all records
All String fields on all records
Configured String fields from Indicator sources that have scores collected
Short (less than 100 characters) String fields on all records

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Text Analytics > Analyzed Fields: Text Analytics analyzes configured String fields from Indicator sources that have scores collected (C). Per p2040: Text Analytics is set up for specific text fields on indicators configured for text indexing — not all journal fields (A) or all string fields (B) on all records. Only the specific string fields enabled in the Text Analytics setup for active indicator sources are processed. Per p1241: only fields with maximum column length of 250 characters are allowed, not all short string fields (D).

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Show multiple elements as property of a widget?

options.text: Apply an Element filter to Breakdown element trends
Control the presentation of multiple element trends
Enable Multi-element select on a Breakdown Dashboard
Allow a widget to follow a Breakdown source

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Widgets > Show Multiple Elements As: The 'Show multiple elements as' property enables multi-element select on a Breakdown Dashboard (C). Per p927: when set to Aggregate, a single aggregated score shows for all selected elements; when set to separate trends, each element shows individually. This property controls how multiple simultaneously-selected breakdown elements are displayed, enabling the multi-element display behavior. Applying an element filter (A) and following a breakdown source (D) are separate widget settings.

questions.stem: When configuring a Breakdown Source on a Dashboard, how do you ensure that Performance Analytics widgets are filtered correctly?

options.text: Edit each widget and enable “Apply Dashboard Filter”
For each widget, enable “Follow interactive filter”
Edit each widget and enable “Follow element”
For each widget, enable “Act as interactive filter”

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdown Dashboards > PA Widget Filtering: When configuring a Breakdown Source on a Dashboard, edit each PA widget and enable 'Follow element' (C) to ensure PA widgets are filtered correctly by the selected breakdown element. Per p1997: 'To have the widget follow the breakdown elements selected on a breakdown dashboard: Select Follow element.' This is distinct from Report widgets which use 'Follow interactive filter' (B). Apply Dashboard Filter (A) does not exist. Act as interactive filter (D) is configured on the filter, not the widget.

questions.stem: How many levels of Breakdowns are available if Collect breakdown matrix is NOT checked on the Indicator?

options.text: 0 - This must be checked to collect Breakdowns.
There is no limit on the levels of Breakdowns collected.
2 - Two levels of Breakdowns are always collected.
1 - Without the matrix, a single level of Breakdowns is collected.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PA > Breakdowns > Matrix Levels: Without 'Collect breakdown matrix' checked on the Indicator, only a single level of Breakdowns is collected (D). Per p840: 'For two levels of breakdown to apply, also select Collect breakdown matrix.' Without the matrix, only the first breakdown level is collected per collection job run. Breakdowns CAN be collected without the matrix (A is wrong — 1 level works). There is no unlimited level option without data snapshots (B is wrong). Two levels require the matrix to be explicitly enabled (C is wrong — 2 levels are not automatically collected).
